idiom_name: hand-built sandbox value (struct of primitive function pointers or a context struct) plus one behaviour entry point per module
implementation_notes: C has no classes, no inheritance and no access control, so the sandbox is built by hand: a behaviour is an ordinary entry point whose parameters are the shared state plus the primitive API, and the primitives are free functions or a struct of function pointers that only the base module implements. Real C code works exactly this way wherever extensions must compose provided operations - a Lua C function receives a lua_State* and may only act through the stack API it is given, and the Linux VFS installs a struct file_operations whose members are the operations a filesystem implements while the kernel drives them. What replaces protected is discipline: the primitives live in the base module, the header that declares them is the published vocabulary, and a second header with the engine internals is kept out of behaviour modules. The hand-built form is still the right choice for a stable plugin ABI with many behaviour modules, because it is the only realisation C offers - but everything the language otherwise checks must be written down and tested by hand.
pitfalls: Nothing prevents a behaviour module from including the engine's internal headers and calling them directly - in C the sandbox wall is a header and review discipline, so a single stray include silently voids the isolation.

The struct of function pointers is the vtable: adding, removing or reordering a primitive changes the layout, so every behaviour module and plugin compiled against the old header must be rebuilt or it will call the wrong member.

A void *ctx plus a function pointer is unchecked: a mismatched cast or an unset member is undefined behaviour rather than a compile error, so validate the whole table at the point where a behaviour is registered and keep one static const table per kind of behaviour.
State has to be threaded explicitly through ctx or stored in globals; globals make the primitives non-reentrant and thread-unsafe, which surfaces only under concurrency.
